newsitem.title: USA: Peru debt recovers, but still lower on week.
newsitem.headline: Peru debt recovers, but still lower on week.

text.p: Peru's when-issued Brady bonds recouped some of the steep losses suffered earlier this week on the hostage situation in Lima, but emerging market debt sources said the prices were still lower on the week.

"Peru prices are not all the way back to where they were but they have recovered some losses," said one market strategist at a U.S. investment bank. He said Peru's PDIs and FLRBs tightened about 10 basis points after widening by at least 50 basis points earlier this week.
At 1615 EST/2115 GMT, Peru's when-issued PDIs were about one percentage point higher at 58-1/2 bid.

Late Tuesday, Peruvian rebels stormed the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima and threatened to kill about 400 hostages, including high-ranking foreign diplomats, unless the government freed jailed comrades of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).

Emerging market debt sources said, however, that volume remained light as activity started to wind down ahead of the Christmas holiday week. Sources said desks are likely to be thinly staffed next week.
In the broader market, Argentine pars were 3/8 firmer at 62-7/8 bid, Venezuelan Pars were 3/4 firmer at 75-3/8 bid and Mexico UMS-26 were 3/8 better at 104-3/4 bid.
Russia's dollar Vnesh were 3/8 higher at 77-1/2 bid and Bulgaria's IABs were 1/2 firmer at 52-1/8 bid.
Looking ahead to 1997, sources said a benign global environment should help to push prices higher in the new year.
"We are pretty positive going into 1997. We might be a little stalled right now but we expect to see a broader distribution of ownership," a source said.

"We've had lower volatility in our market and we've had very strong returns this year so the longer that lasts and the more people get wind of it, the more they will be attracted to our market," the source added.
